findings.highlight: my life has just been trying to overturn those words.
findings.evidenceJa: その言葉を覆す為だけのもの、だったのかもしれない。
findings.governingReading: He thinks that perhaps all his time since Kiritsugu’s words was spent trying to overturn them.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s tentative interpretation of his life becomes settled biography.

findings.highlight: I can't look away from his final moment.
findings.evidenceJa: その最期に、背を向ける事はできない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot turn his back on Kiritsugu’s end and what the relieved final words entrusted to him.
findings.explanation: Refusing to turn his back on Kiritsugu’s final trust becomes not looking away from the moment.

findings.highlight: So that he doesn't approve of the former Shirou Emiya.
findings.evidenceJa: あいつがかつての衛宮士郎を認めないように。
findings.governingReading: Shirou denies Archer just as Archer refuses to acknowledge the former Emiya Shirou; the two rejections mirror one another.
findings.explanation: A mirror comparison becomes a purpose clause.

findings.governingReading: The fragment breaks after “never, to myself alone—,” leaving readers to infer that the self who chose belief must not deny it.
findings.explanation: The unfinished vow loses its self-directed object.

findings.highlight: The Magic Circuit that I overused is still exhausted
findings.evidenceJa: あれだけ酷使した魔術回路はさすがに消耗したままだが
findings.governingReading: His bodily sensations and headache recover, but the Magic Circuits he overused remain depleted without having burned out.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s exhausted Magic Circuits become one exhausted circuit.

findings.evidenceJa: があー、とランサーを責め立てるセイバー。
findings.governingReading: Still heated, Saber bears down on Lancer with a drawn-out angry cry and reproaches him at length.
findings.explanation: Saber loudly berating Lancer becomes merely accusing him.
